items.reason: Closing a strategy shuts down the factory-shared pool, so subsequent strategies reuse dead queues and commit unprocessed messages.
Unbounded queues and missing backpressure allow the backlog to grow without limit when workers fall behind.
The offset scan requires consecutive integers, causing legitimate Kafka offset gaps to block commit progress.
The test checks for absent commits before the one-second commit loop fires, so it fails to detect failed offsets being committed. It also notes the related docstring contradiction.
The documented backpressure guarantee is absent because the queues are unbounded and submissions do not apply backpressure.
The worker completes offsets in finally even when processing fails, contradicting the successful-processing commit guarantee.
Strategy shutdown destroys the shared factory pool, causing post-rebalance submissions to fail and unprocessed offsets to be committed.
The comment identifies the consecutive-integer offset scan and stale tracking state across rebalances as causes of stalled commits.
The next strategy reuses a pool shut down by the previous strategy, and enqueue failures are converted into completed offsets.
Shutting down the factory-shared pool from the strategy causes post-rebalance messages to be committed without processing.
The test promises continued commits after errors but asserts no commits occurred; it should wait for and assert the positive commit behavior.
The ordering test checks only the processed count, so out-of-order processing would still pass.
